_note: The ONLY place this app may disagree with vendor/agency-agents/tools.json. scripts/sync-vendor.mjs merges these fields into the generated src-tauri/data/tools.json; a field that duplicates upstream fails the build (dead override), an unknown field fails the build (typo), and a test names every entry. Keep each `_why` next to its value: the reason is part of the contract. Paths are relative to $HOME, exactly like the rest of `detect.dirs`.

gemini-cli._why: Upstream lists `.gemini/agents`, which is where Gemini CLI READS agents. Detection has to fire for a user who has the CLI but no agents directory yet, so the app tests the CLI's home (`.gemini`). `agentsDir` still points at the real read path.

antigravity._why: Upstream lists the two agent DESTINATION dirs (`.gemini/config/agents`, `.agents/agents`), which only exist after someone installs agents. Detection must recognise the three Antigravity surfaces themselves — the App (`.gemini/antigravity`), the CLI and the IDE — and they can coexist, so all three are listed. `agentsDir` still points at the real read path.

kimi._why: Upstream declares no detection roots at all for Kimi. The app can still recognise the CLI's config home, which is what the Tools view needs to report it as present.

pi-agent._why: Upstream lists `.pi/agent/agents`, the agent read path. Detection uses the CLI home (`.pi`) so a fresh install with no agents directory is still recognised.

oh-my-pi._why: Upstream lists `.omp/agent/agents`, the agent read path. Detection uses the CLI home (`.omp`) so a fresh install with no agents directory is still recognised.
